<noinclude><pagequality level="1" user="" /></noinclude><section begin=par159 />''if thou will save'', &c.; {{GHGbible-ref|book=Gn|chapter=24|verse=49}} {{GHGheb|text=אִם־יֶשְׁבֶם עֹשִׂים|translate=if ye will deal}}, &c.; {{GHGbible-ref|book=1 S|chapter=23|verse=23}}. In {{GHGbible-ref|book=Gn|chapter=24|verse=42}} f. the condition is expressed in a more humble form by the addition of {{GHGheb|text=נָא}}. With {{GHGheb|text=אֵין}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Gn|chapter=43|verse=5}} {{GHGheb|text=וְאִם־אֵֽינְךָ מְשַׁלֵּחַ|translate=but if thou wilt not send}}, &c.; 20:7 (with imperative in the apodosis); {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ex|chapter=8|verse=17}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ex|chapter=9|verse=2|hidebook=1}} f., {{GHGbible-ref|book=1 S|chapter=19|verse=11}} (all with a participle also in the apodosis). But {{GHGheb|text=יֵשׁ}} and {{GHGheb|text=אַ֫יִן}} may also be used after {{GHGheb|text=אִם}} without a suffix; thus {{GHGheb|text=יֵשׁ}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Gn|chapter=23|verse=8}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=1 S|chapter=20|verse=8}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=2 K|chapter=9|verse=15}}, &c., {{GHGheb|text=אִם־אַ֫יִן}} (''if it be not the case'') {{GHGbible-ref|book=Gn|chapter=30|verse=1}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ex|chapter=32|verse=32}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ju|chapter=9|verse=15}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=2 K|chapter=2|verse=10}}; cf. also {{GHGheb|text=אִם־כֵּן|translate=if it be so}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Gn|chapter=25|verse=22}}.

{{GHGmargin-letter|159|w}}
'''B.''' {{GHGheb|text=הֵן|translate=if}}, generally supposed to be originally identical with {{GHGheb|text=הֵן|translate=behold!}}<ref>There could be no doubt of their identity if {{GHGheb|text=וְהִנֵּה}} in {{GHGbible-ref|book=1 S|chapter=9|verse=7}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=2 S|chapter=18|verse=11}}, simply meant ''if''. We must, however, keep to the meaning ''but behold''.</ref> Probably, however, {{GHGheb|text=הֵן|translate=if}}, is a pure Aramaism, and since the Aramaic word never has the meaning ''behold'', it is at least improbable that it had originally any connexion with {{GHGheb|text=הֵן}} or {{GHGheb|text=הִנֵּה}}. Cf. {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ex|chapter=8|verse=22}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Lv|chapter=25|verse=20}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Is|chapter=54|verse=15}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Jer|chapter=3|verse=1}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Hag|chapter=2|verse=12}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=2 Ch|chapter=7|verse=13}}, and frequently in Job, as {{GHGbible-ref|book=Jb|chapter=9|verse=11|hidebook=1}}, 12, 12:14, 15, 19:7, 23:8, 40:23, always with wāw apodosis following, except in 13:15, where consequently the meaning ''see'' is no doubt preferable.

{{GHGmargin-letter|159|x}}
'''C.''' {{GHGheb|text=לוּ|translate=if}}, {{GHGheb|text=לוּלֵא}} ({{GHGheb|text=לוּלֵי}}) ''if not''.

1. With {{GHGterm|perfect}} in the protasis and apodosis (cf. {{GHGpar|106|p}}), e.g. {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ju|chapter=8|verse=19}}; {{GHGheb|text=אִלּוּ}} is used in the same sense as {{GHGheb|text=לוּ}} in {{GHGbible-ref|book=Est|chapter=7|verse=4}}, cf. {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ec|chapter=6|verse=6}} (with a question in the apodosis).—With the perfect in protasis and apodosis after {{GHGheb|text=לוּלֵא}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Gn|chapter=31|verse=42}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Gn|chapter=43|verse=10|hidebook=1}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ju|chapter=14|verse=18}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=1 S|chapter=25|verse=34}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=2 S|chapter=2|verse=27}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Is|chapter=1|verse=9}}. On the other hand, in {{GHGbible-ref|book=Dt|chapter=32|verse=29}} {{GHGheb|text=לוּ}} with a perfect is followed by an imperfect in the apodosis, ''if they were wise, they would understand this''; in {{GHGbible-ref|book=Mi|chapter=2|verse=11}} by a perfect consecutive.

{{GHGmargin-letter|159|y}}
2. With {{GHGterm|imperfect}} after {{GHGheb|text=לוּלֵא}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Dt|chapter=32|verse=27}}, {{GHGheb|text=אָגוּר}} probably as the ''modus rei repetitae, were it not that I ever and again feared'', &c.; so also the imperfect after {{GHGheb|text=לוּ}} with the apodosis suppressed, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Gn|chapter=50|verse=15}} ''supposing that Joseph should hate us''; since, according to the context, the danger was real, the use of {{GHGheb|text=לוּ}} here is strange; conversely in other cases, e.g. {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ps|chapter=73|verse=15}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Jb|chapter=9|verse=15}} f. 30, {{GHGheb|text=לוּ}} would be more natural than {{GHGheb|text=אִם}}.

{{GHGmargin-letter|159|z}}
3. A noun-clause occurs after {{GHGheb|text=לוּ}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=2 S|chapter=18|verse=12}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=2 K|chapter=3|verse=14}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ps|chapter=81|verse=14}}, all with imperfect in the apodosis; {{GHGbible-ref|book=Jb|chapter=16|verse=4}} {{GHGheb|text=לוּ יֵשׁ}}, with cohortative in the apodosis.

'''D.''' {{GHGheb|text=כִּי|translate=supposing that, if}}:—

{{GHGmargin-letter|159|aa}}
1. {{GHGheb|text=כִּי}} with {{GHGterm|perfect}} in the protasis, e.g. {{GHGbible-ref|book=Nu|chapter=5|verse=20}} {{GHGheb|text=וְאַתְּ כִּי שָׂטִית|translate=but thou, if thou hast gone astray}}, &c.; with a frequentative perfect consecutive in the apodosis, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Jb|chapter=7|verse=13}} f.; with an imperfect consecutive, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Jb|chapter=22|verse=29}}.

{{GHGmargin-letter|159|bb}}
2. {{GHGheb|text=כִּי}} with {{GHGterm|imperfect}} in the protasis, e.g. {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ps|chapter=23|verse=4}} {{GHGheb|text=גַּם כִּֽי־אֵלֵךְ|translate=yea, though I walk}} (have to walk)..., ''I will fear no'' ({{GHGheb|text=לֹֽא־אִירָא}}) ''evil''; 37:24; {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ex|chapter=21|verse=2}} {{GHGheb|text=כִּֽי־תִקְנֶה עֶ֫בֶד עִבְרִי וג׳|translate=if thou buy an Hebrew servant, six years shall he serve}} (but in verses 3–5 a series of definite conditions with definite consequences is introduced by {{GHGheb|text=אִם}}; so also the {{GHGheb|text=כִּי}} in verse 7 is followed in verses 8–11 by the special cases with {{GHGheb|text=אִם}}; cf. also verse 17 ff.); cf. {{GHGbible-ref|book=Gn|chapter=4|verse=24}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Gn|chapter=24|verse=41|hidebook=1}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Jb|chapter=38|verse=5}}; with a perfect consecutive in the apodosis, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Gn|chapter=32|verse=18}} f., {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ex|chapter=18|verse=16}}; with a noun-clause, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Is|chapter=1|verse=15}}.

3. {{GHGheb|text=כִּי}} with a ''noun-clause'' (and imperfect in the apodosis), {{GHGbible-ref|book=2 S|chapter=19|verse=8}}.

{{center|{{Small-caps|Remarks.}}}}

{{GHGmargin-letter|159|cc}}
1. In {{GHGbible-ref|book=2 K|chapter=5|verse=13}} the particle {{GHGheb|text=אבי}} (Masora {{GHGheb|text=אָבִי}}, probably in the sense of ''my father'') appears exceptionally for {{GHGheb|text=לוּ}}; its meaning here is unquestionable, but<section end=par159 /><noinclude>
<references/></noinclude>
